name: Representation and Kernel Modifications
text:
# Representation and Kernel Modifications

Also called: Kernel Variants, Primitive Representation Extensions

## Overview
Representation and Kernel Modifications extend the standard [3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)](#1174-3d-gaussian-splatting-3dgs.md) primitive definition and rendering kernel to address specific limitations in shape modeling, geometric consistency, memory efficiency, and optical effects. While standard 3DGS relies on positive-only, isotropic/anisotropic Gaussian blobs with exponential decay, this family introduces negative color contributions [9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md], voxel-based scaffolds for attribute prediction [9186-scaffold-gs.md], tangent-plane densification for geometric smoothness [9187-geogaussian.md], non-exponential decaying kernels [9911-darbf-splatting.md], and spatially-varying blur kernels [14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md]. These methods solve issues such as the inability to model complex nonlinear structures (e.g., donuts, thin spokes) [9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md, S2], inefficient memory usage in sparse regions [9186-scaffold-gs.md], geometric artifacts during densification [9187-geogaussian.md], and the lack of closed-form integration for non-Gaussian kernels [9911-darbf-splatting.md].

## Shared principles
All methods in this family retain the core differentiable rasterization pipeline of 3DGS but modify one or more of the following components:
1.  **Primitive Attributes:** The tuple defining a Gaussian primitive is extended or reinterpreted. Standard attributes include position $\mathbf{p}$, covariance $\Sigma$, opacity $\alpha$, and color $\mathbf{c}$ (often via [Spherical Harmonics](#5603-spherical-harmonics.md)). Modifications include allowing negative color values [9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md], decoupling attributes from direct storage by mapping voxel features to attributes via neural networks [9186-scaffold-gs.md], or adding learnable oriented normals [S2].
2.  **Kernel Function:** The function $K(\mathbf{x})$ used to weight the contribution of a primitive at a pixel $\mathbf{x}$ is replaced or augmented. Standard 3DGS uses the Gaussian PDF. Alternatives include Decaying Anisotropic Radial Basis Functions (DARBFs) like Half-Cosine or [Inverse Multiquadric](#9910-inverse-multiquadric-splatting.md) [9911-darbf-splatting.md], or spatially-varying blur kernels selected from a grid based on sharpness priors [14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md].
3.  **Densification and Initialization:** The strategy for adding new primitives is modified to respect [geometric constraints](#8727-depth-and-geometry-supervision.md) (e.g., [tangent plane projection](#3311-optimal-gaussian-splatting-projection.md) [9187-geogaussian.md]) or structural priors (e.g., voxel grid scaffolding [9186-scaffold-gs.md]).
4.  **Integration Shortcut:** Standard 3DGS relies on the closed-form integral of the Gaussian projection. Methods using non-Gaussian kernels [9911-darbf-splatting.md] or oriented surface assumptions [S2] must derive or approximate new integration shortcuts or correction factors to maintain rasterization efficiency.

## Subtopics

### [Negative Gaussian Splatting](9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md)
A variant that extends the [primitive representation](#11838-primitive-representation.md) by incorporating "negative Gaussians"—ellipsoids with negative color values—into the optimization process [9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md]. It solves the limitation of standard [Gaussian Splatting](#946-gaussian-splatting.md), which relies on positive-only components to model complex nonlinear structures and high-frequency elements, often requiring a large number of primitives and increasing time complexity [9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md]. By allowing positive and negative Gaussians to cancel each other out, NegGS provides greater flexibility in shape representation and color modulation, particularly for rapid color transitions and shadows [9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md]. It interprets the [interaction](#41-interaction.md) between two Gaussians as a "Diff-Gaussian" distribution, defined by the ratio of their probability density functions (PDFs) [9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md]. Choose this method when rendering scenes with complex internal structures, thin filaments, or high-frequency color variations that standard positive-only Gaussians struggle to represent efficiently. See [9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md].

### [Scaffold-GS](9186-scaffold-gs.md)
A representation modification that replaces the direct parameterization of Gaussian attributes with a voxel-based neural field [9186-scaffold-gs.md]. It solves the issue of inefficient memory usage and poor initialization in sparse regions by decoupling the geometric scaffold (voxels) from the radiance attributes (Gaussians) [9186-scaffold-gs.md]. Unlike standard 3DGS which stores attributes directly per Gaussian, [Scaffold-GS](#9186-scaffold-gs.md) determines all Gaussian attributes via interpolated features from a voxel grid and lightweight neural networks, enabling a more compact and structured representation [9186-scaffold-gs.md]. Choose this method when memory efficiency is critical or when the scene has large empty regions where standard densification would waste resources. See [9186-scaffold-gs.md].

### [GeoGaussian](9187-geogaussian.md)
A [training optimization and initialization](#13464-training-optimization-and-initialization.md) strategy that improves geometric consistency by densifying primitives on the tangent plane of existing Gaussians and enforcing smoothness of geometric properties between neighboring Gaussians [9187-geogaussian.md]. It distinguishes itself from sibling methods like [Negative Gaussian Splatting](#9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md) or Scaffold-GS by focusing specifically on the spatial distribution and geometric coherence of the Gaussian primitives during the densification phase, rather than modifying the kernel function or using scaffold structures [9187-geogaussian.md]. Choose this method when high-fidelity surface reconstruction and geometric smoothness are prioritized over raw photometric accuracy. See [9187-geogaussian.md].

### [DARBF-Splatting](9911-darbf-splatting.md)
A method for [differentiable volume rendering](#43-differentiable-volume-rendering.md) that replaces the standard Gaussian reconstruction kernels of 3D Gaussian Splatting with a broader class of non-exponential functions called Decaying Anisotropic Radial Basis Functions (DARBFs) [9911-darbf-splatting.md]. It solves the limitation of [splatting](#23-splatting.md) methods being restricted to the exponential family by enabling the use of kernels such as half-cosine and inverse multiquadric, which offer faster training convergence and lower memory usage while maintaining comparable visual quality [9911-darbf-splatting.md]. Unlike its siblings, it introduces a scalar correction factor to approximate the closed-form integration shortcut inherent to Gaussians, allowing efficient rasterization of these alternative kernels [9911-darbf-splatting.md]. Choose this method when faster convergence or specific kernel shapes (e.g., finite support) are desired. See [9911-darbf-splatting.md].

### [Grid-based Blur Kernel](14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md)
A method that replaces MLP-generated blur kernels with a learnable, spatially-indexed grid to model spatially-varying blurriness in radiance field optimization [14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md]. Unlike siblings that modify [primitive geometry](#6264-primitive-geometry.md) or negative contributions, this method explicitly handles defocus blur by assigning one of $N_k$ trainable kernels to pixels based on a sharpness prior, improving reconstruction quality in defocused regions without increasing kernel generation cost [14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md]. Choose this method when reconstructing scenes with significant depth-of-field effects or defocus blur. See [14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md].

### Gaussian Shell Maps
Combines CNN-based generators with 3DGS to recreate virtual humans with sophisticated details such as clothing and accessories [S1].

### Gaussian Wrapping
A framework that reinterprets 3D Gaussian primitives as oriented probabilistic surface elements representing geometry only within an oriented half-space, allowing derivation of closed-form occupancy, vacancy, and normal fields for watertight mesh extraction [S2]. Model surface points with asymmetric primitives where the Gaussian models density decay on the outward-facing side, while the inward-facing side is considered fully occupied [S2]. Identify geometric gaps where the oriented surface assumption is violated and densify the representation to obtain a watertight shell of oriented primitives [S2]. Introduce a learnable oriented normal at each Gaussian element and define an adapted attenuation formulation to enable closed-form expressions for normal and occupancy fields [S2]. Introduce a novel consistency loss and a dedicated [densification strategy](#6234-densification-strategy.md) to enforce Gaussians to wrap the entire surface by closing geometric holes [S2]. Modify the differentiable rasterizer to output depth as an isosurface of the continuous model [S2]. Use Primal Adaptive Meshing for Region-of-Interest meshing at arbitrary resolution [S2].

## Background
The standard 3D Gaussian Splatting method [Parent] established a baseline for fast, high-quality novel view synthesis using explicit Gaussian primitives. However, limitations in representation (positive-only colors, symmetric blobs) and kernel properties (exponential decay) motivated extensions. Negative Gaussian Splatting [9152-negative-gaussian-splatting.md] and [DARBF-Splatting](#9911-darbf-splatting.md) [9911-darbf-splatting.md] address the kernel and color representation limits. Scaffold-GS [9186-scaffold-gs.md] and [GeoGaussian](#9187-geogaussian.md) [9187-geogaussian.md] address geometric and memory efficiency. Gaussian Wrapping [S2] adapts the primitives for surface reconstruction. Grid-based Blur Kernels [14244-grid-based-blur-kernel.md] address optical defocus. Gaussian Shell Maps [S1] and Gaussian Wrapping [S2] are specifically noted for human/avatar and surface reconstruction applications.
